request.user:
Subject: Physics
Question type: integer answer (no options)

Two wheels each marked with a dot on its rim are mounted side by side. When the wheels are at rest, the dots are aligned. One wheel is given a constant angular acceleration of π/2 r a d / s e c^2 and the other is given a constant angular acceleration of π/4 r a d / s e c^2 . The time after which the two dots will be aligned again for the first time (in seconds) is

result.working: Both wheels start from rest and rotate in the same sense. θ1 = (1/2)(π/2)t² and θ2 = (1/2)(π/4)t². The dots line up again for the first time when the faster wheel has gained one full turn: θ1 − θ2 = 2π. This gives (1/2)(π/4)t² = 2π, so πt²/8 = 2π. Then t² = 16, so t = 4 s.
result.note: The question does not state the sense of rotation; I assumed both wheels turn the same way. If they turned in opposite senses, (1/2)(3π/4)t² = 2π would give t ≈ 2.31 s, which is not an integer.
